en: The Discourse Connected with the Fourth Nibbāna.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Blessed One was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk concerning Nibbāna.
And those bhikkhus, having applied their whole minds and given full attention, were listening to the Dhamma with eager ears.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For one who is dependent, there is wavering; for one who is independent, there is no wavering.
When there is no wavering, there is tranquility.”
When there is tranquility, there is no inclination.
When there is no inclination, there is no coming and going.
When there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and reappearing.
When there is no cutting off and reappearing, there is neither here nor beyond, nor in between the two.
This indeed is the end of suffering. Thus ends the fourth [discourse].
